podcast.title: Early Life and Education
podcast.body: Grew up in Guelph, Ontario. Played the flute in his school band, which he described as a "real rough time," motivating him to pick up the electric guitar. Attended McMaster University, also studying Political Science, similar to Max Kermann, seeking a new social experience and to meet people. "Yeah, I grew up in Gualfantario. And similarly, I played in high school with friends. I played in the school band. And that was, I played the flute. It was a real rough time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: First Impression of Max Kermann
podcast.body: Mike DeAngeles met Max Kermann on the first day of university, describing Max as having a lot of "outward energy" and wearing a "funny like conductors hat." Mike recognized Max's potential as a frontman, a role Mike himself was uncomfortable with in his high school band. "And when I met Max, he's not lying when he sort of like half pushed me over. And he was wearing a really funny like conductors hat and just had a lot of like this sort of like outward energy that I noticed right away as, hey, maybe a good guy to be a front man."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: University Jobs and Firing
podcast.body: During his university summers, Mike held "terrible" temp jobs, including picking up needles on top of Jackson Square and working in a distribution warehouse. He was also fired from East Side Marios, a moment Max Kermann called him about immediately after they met. "I got fired as a waiter. The job was fine. I was probably deserving of the firing. Max called me right after we met for a drink."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Band Formation at McMaster University (2004)
xref.body: The band's core began forming on the first and second days Max Kermann attended McMaster University in Hamilton in 2004. Max, who was primarily interested in finding bandmates, met Mike DeAngeles on day one by asking about his favorite bands (The Weakerthans) and if he played guitar. On day two, Nick Dica introduced himself to Max because Max was wearing a Sam Roberts Band T-shirt, and upon learning Nick played bass, he was also invited to join. "You're literally the first and second day that you were in university."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Arkells - In Their Own Words: Part 1

xref.title: Name Change to Arkells (Late 2007/Early 2008)
xref.body: The name change from Charlemagne to Arkells occurred under extreme pressure when Dino Lone Records needed a new name in 45 minutes for an EP flyer to be inserted into the City and Colour record. Max Kermann and Mike DeAngeles, who lived on Arkell Street at the time, proposed the name in a last-minute effort, noting its 60s Motown-esque sound. "So then we frantically got on the phone. I was at the library and McMaster, I still remember. And we called everyone, we got to change the name now because we've been sitting on this kind of decision for a long time and we just hadn't got around to it."

xref.title: Band Recruiting Strategy at McMaster
xref.body: On his first day at McMaster University, Max Kermann proactively sought out potential band members. He met Mike DeAngeles by asking about his favorite bands and instruments. On the second day, Nick Dica approached him because of his Sam Roberts Band T-shirt, and Max quickly recruited him for bass. "I did immediately start profiling people on campus and seeing, this is like the kind of person that would want to be in a band with me. And on the first day I met Mike and on the second day I met Nick."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Education and Entry into Arkells
xref.body: Dan Griffith attended McMaster University with Max Kermann, Mike DeAngeles, and Nick Dica. He joined Arkells a little after the initial trio started jamming, becoming their keyboard player until he left to go back to school. "So Dan went to Mac with us. Okay. And he joined the band a little after the three of us started jamming and with our original drummer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Mike DeAngeles' Favorite Band
xref.body: The Weakerthans, a band from Winnipeg, were Mike DeAngeles's favorite band when he met Max Kermann on the first day of university. Their album had just been released, and Mike had recently seen them in Hamilton, leading to his obsession with their music. "He said, yeah, I'm into this band. You probably haven't heard of them. They're from Winnipeg. They're called The Weaker Thens. And they were my favorite band at the time."
